evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant woman with severe nausea and vomiting: assessment with the PUQE score, admission criteria, stepwise antiemetics, intravenous fluids, thiamine, thromboprophylaxis and corticosteroids, using RCOG Green-top Guideline 69 and a Scottish health board guideline.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The RCOG text opened gave no doses (it refers to an appendix not included); doses come from the NHS Borders guideline version 1.0.
Thiamine IV regimen detail, low-molecular-weight heparin dose by weight, potassium dose and admission and discharge criteria in the Borders guideline were not found; LMWH dose is not given here.
The PUQE-24 bands in NHS Borders list 'Mild: 6'; the RCOG Appendix II bands were not opened.
No Saudi guideline was opened. No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics and Gynaecology guideline was opened.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Ketonuria is not an indicator of dehydration and should not be used to assess severity. Weight loss of 5% or more of pre-pregnancy weight is a sign of significant disease. Thiamine deficiency with dextrose-containing fluids can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy. Corticosteroids are reserved for cases where intravenous fluids and regular antiemetics have failed.
keyMechanisms: Ketonuria is not an indicator of dehydration and should not be used to assess severity.
Weight loss of 5% or more of pre-pregnancy weight is a sign of significant disease.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess
actions: PUQE-24, weight change, hydration and exclude comorbidity.

clinicalManagement.title: First-line antiemetics
actions: Doxylamine-pyridoxine, cyclizine, prochlorperazine or promethazine; do not suggest ginger (no efficacy shown and may worsen symptoms).

clinicalManagement.title: Second line
actions: Metoclopramide (maximum 30 mg in 24 hours, up to 5 days) or ondansetron (very small absolute increase in orofacial clefting risk in the first trimester).

clinicalManagement.title: Admit and rehydrate
actions: Normal saline with potassium; avoid dextrose-containing fluids without thiamine.
Give thiamine to all women admitted with vomiting; offer low-molecular-weight heparin to women admitted with hyperemesis.

clinicalManagement.title: Third line
actions: Hydrocortisone 100 mg twice daily intravenously then prednisolone 40 to 50 mg daily, tapering by 5 to 10 mg per week to the lowest effective dose.

regimens.indication: First-line antiemetic for mild to moderate nausea and vomiting
regimens.dose: 20/20 mg at night, increasing to 10/10 mg in the morning and 10/10 mg at lunchtime if required
regimens.frequency: At night with optional morning and lunchtime doses
adjustments: The only licensed treatment for nausea and vomiting in pregnancy in the UK (10 mg doxylamine succinate and 10 mg pyridoxine hydrochloride delayed-release).
contraindications: Ask about previous adverse reactions and stop promptly if they occur.

regimens.indication: Prevention of Wernicke encephalopathy in vomiting or reduced intake
regimens.patientGroup: Women admitted with vomiting or severely reduced intake
regimens.dose: 100 mg orally three times daily, or parenteral thiamine about 100 mg as part of vitamin B complex (Pabrinex)
regimens.duration: While vomiting or reduced intake continues, especially before dextrose or parenteral nutrition
adjustments: Avoid dextrose-containing fluids without thiamine cover.
contraindications: No contraindications are listed in the source opened.

regimens.indication: Third-line treatment when fluids and antiemetics have failed
regimens.dose: Hydrocortisone 100 mg twice daily, then prednisolone 40 to 50 mg daily
regimens.duration: Taper by 5 to 10 mg per week to the lowest effective maintenance dose; continue until gestation at which hyperemesis usually resolves
monitoring: Blood pressure; screen for gestational diabetes.
contraindications: Reserve for failure of intravenous fluids and regular antiemetics.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: PUQE-24 total (Pregnancy-Unique Quantification of Emesis, sum of three questions)
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Mild 6; moderate 7 to 12; severe 13 to 15 (NHS Borders).
Continued vomiting with clinical dehydration or weight loss over 5% despite oral antiemetics.
